official.deadline_note: YTB publishes a General Application Period of 10 January - 20 February every year in its Application Calendar; the 2026 joint-programme window ran 10 January - 20 February 2026 and closed. The 2027 date itself is not yet published, so this is the annually repeating window, not a confirmed 2027 date.
official.application_cycle: Annual general application window of 10 January - 20 February; the 2026 cycle ran 10 January - 20 February 2026 for 2026/2027 entry. Published downstream calendar: evaluation March-April, interviews April-June, results early August, initial procedures August, transfers of grantees to Turkiye September. The next window is expected January-February 2027 and will be confirmed on the official announcements page.
official.status_note: The 2026 application period (10 January - 20 February 2026) has closed; the latest official activity is the February 2026 YTB-IsDB programme implementation meeting. The Application Calendar lists 10 January - 20 February as the application period every year, so the next round opens in January 2027.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The programme 'covers ... tuition fees'; the awarding body states: 'While studying at the most prestigious universities at world standards, your university tuition is covered by Turkiye Scholarships.'
benefits: Monthly stipend: 6.500 TL at Associate's and Bachelor's levels, 9.500 TL at Master's level and 13.000 TL at PhD level per month (the recorded figure is the Master's-level amount)

Accommodation support: dormitory fees covered for the duration of studies at undergraduate level; master's and doctoral students get dormitory right in the first year and then a housing allowance of 6.000 TL per month in Istanbul and Ankara and 5.000 TL per month in other cities
One-year Turkish language course at university Turkish Teaching Centers (TÖMER)
One-time round-trip flight ticket (at the beginning of education and when graduating), plus university and department placement and access to the Türkiye Alumni Network
eligibility: Open to successful international students from IsDB member countries and Muslim communities around the world; Turkish citizens and individuals who have lost Turkish citizenship are ineligible
Minimum academic achievement of 70% for associate and bachelor's degree candidates, 75% for graduate candidates, and 90% for candidates of Health Sciences (Medicine, Dentistry and Pharmacy)
Age criteria: under 21 years of age for associate and bachelor's degree programmes, under 30 for master's programmes, under 35 for PhD programmes
Graduates or those who will graduate at the end of the current academic year (before August)
Not currently enrolled in a programme at a Turkish university at the level of education applied for

Restricted to the departments, universities and countries published in the official IsDB joint programme lists: associate, bachelor's and M.Sc. tracks are for IsDB Least Developed Member Countries, and the PhD track (Merit Scholarship Programme for High Technology) is for the wider listed IsDB member countries
requirements: Apply only through the Türkiye Scholarships official website (Türkiye Scholarships Application System, TBBS)
Select 'Yes' under the 'Joint Scholarship Programs' section on the application screen in order to be considered for the joint programme
Choose a programme and department from the published list of eligible fields of study and countries for the relevant level
Meet the minimum academic achievement and age criteria for the level applied for
documents: A valid identity document, ID card or passport; and a photograph of the candidate taken within the last 1 year
Diploma or temporary graduation certificate, plus transcript, for the latest completed education
International exam results (GRE, GMAT, SAT, etc.) if required by the chosen university or programme
International language test results such as TOEFL or DELF if required by the chosen university or programme
A proposal for a research topic and a written example of the research carried out (only for PhD applications)
selection_criteria: Preliminary assessment on minimum academic achievement, age limits set for each level of education, and required documents
Expert evaluation of academic status, previous qualifications, academic interests, career goals, consistency of preferences, content of the letter of intent, and participation in social activities
A 30-question quantitative test (mathematics, geometry and logic) for undergraduate candidates before the face-to-face interviews

Face-to-face interview of usually 15-30 minutes before interview committees of academics and experts, including a document check and questions on the purpose of the application, academic knowledge and career goals
Final assessment by a selection committee that creates the list of applicants who will receive scholarships
coverage: Accommodation support (dormitory fees, or a housing allowance after the first year at graduate level)
application_method: Register on the Türkiye Scholarships Application System (TBBS) at https://tbbs.turkiyeburslari.gov.tr
Select 'Yes' under the 'Joint Scholarship Programs' section on the application screen
Choose an eligible programme, department and country from the published list for the level applied for
Upload all required documents and submit the application within the published window (10 January - 20 February)
official.application_route: One standard online application through the Türkiye Scholarships Application System (TBBS), answering 'Yes' to the Joint Scholarship Programs section - there is no separate IsDB application form.
official.citizenship_residency: Turkish citizens and individuals who have lost Turkish citizenship are ineligible; the programme is for international students from IsDB member countries and Muslim communities living in other countries. Actual eligibility is further narrowed by the level-specific official country lists (IsDB Least Developed Member Countries for the associate, bachelor's and M.Sc. tracks; a wider list of IsDB member countries for the PhD track).
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the programme is designed for international students only; Turkish citizens and former Turkish citizens cannot apply.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Candidates may only apply to the universities, departments and countries published in the official IsDB joint programme lists. The tracks are titled: IsDB Joint Scholarship Program for Associate Degree / for Bachelor Degree / for Master of Science (M.Sc.), each for IsDB Least Developed Member Countries (LDMCs), and the IsDB Joint Scholarship Program Merit Scholarship Programme for High Technology (PhD) for IsDB member countries, with fields such as pharmaceutical chemistry, analytical chemistry, biophysics and computer engineering, taught in Turkish or English.
official.research_requirement: PhD applicants only: a proposal for a research topic and a written example of the research they have carried out must be uploaded.
official.duration: A 1-year Turkish language preparatory programme plus the normal duration of the programme: two-year associate degree programmes; four-year bachelor's programmes (five years for Dentistry, six years for Medicine); two-year graduate (master's) programme; four-year doctoral programme. An additional year at most may be granted for completion (up to two years for medicine, dentistry and pharmacy), with the monthly stipend subject to a 50% deduction during the extension.
official.description: A joint scholarship programme co-funded by the Presidency for Turks Abroad and Related Communities (YTB) and the Islamic Development Bank (IsDB) since 2020, enabling high-achieving students from IsDB member countries and Muslim communities living in other countries to receive education at internationally recognized universities in Türkiye. It is offered at Associate, Bachelor, Master's and PhD level and covers a monthly stipend, accommodation support, tuition fees, health insurance, a one-year Turkish language course and a one-time round-trip airfare. Associate and bachelor's degree students are required to repay the loan after graduation and employment, in easy installments, to the IsDB Education Trust (IET), a Waqf set up in the students' countries.
official.region: Türkiye (country of study); candidates from IsDB member countries and Muslim communities worldwide
official.program_type: Joint scholarship programme of Türkiye Scholarships co-funded by YTB and the Islamic Development Bank; LDMC-restricted associate, bachelor's and M.Sc. tracks plus a High Technology PhD track, with a repayment obligation at associate and bachelor's level
official.english_requirement: No single programme-wide score is published. Many programmes are taught in Turkish, and where a chosen university or programme is taught in English the candidate must provide an internationally accepted language proficiency certificate (TOEFL or other equivalent certification if the university officially states it acceptable); most such programmes also require international admission test results (GRE, GMAT, SAT). Candidates sitting the undergraduate selection test are expected to demonstrate a sufficient level of English to comprehend English-language questions. All awardees without a C1 Turkish proficiency certificate, including those placed in English-medium programmes, must attend the 1-year Turkish language course and attain C1.

verification.notes: Amounts, coverage, criteria, documents, selection process, durations and application route were taken from YTB's own turkiyeburslari.gov.tr pages and the two official PDFs published on that domain; all were reachable and read in full on 2026-10-10.

applicant_utility.summary: This is the IsDB route into Turkiye Scholarships: you file one standard TBBS application and tick 'Yes' in the Joint Scholarship Programs section, so the joint track adds no separate paperwork, but it also means you are judged on the same academic merits and interview as every other Türkiye Scholarships candidate. The window is only about six weeks long (10 January to 20 February) and results are not announced until early August, so treat the cycle as a full-year commitment rather than a parallel application. Read the level-specific country list before falling in love with the programme: the announcement text says 'IsDB member countries and Muslim communities', but the official list restricts the associate, bachelor's and M.Sc. tracks to IsDB Least Developed Member Countries, while only the High Technology PhD track opens to a much wider IsDB membership. Master's and PhD awardees carry no repayment clause; associate and bachelor's awardees should treat the award as a soft loan repayable to the IsDB Education Trust after they graduate and find employment.
applicant_utility.best_fit: High-scoring graduates of IsDB Least Developed Member Countries (70%+ for undergraduate, 75%+ for graduate) and PhD applicants from listed IsDB member countries in high-technology fields who want a fully supported year of Turkish language study before their degree.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your exact country appears on the official list for your exact level before preparing anything else - the LDMC lists are narrower than the PhD list and narrower than the announcement wording suggests
Scan and, where needed, translate your diploma, transcript and identity document before 10 January, because the upload must be complete inside the six-week window
Check the language of instruction of every programme you shortlist inside TBBS and book a TOEFL/equivalent (and GRE/GMAT/SAT where required) early if any programme is English-taught
As an undergraduate candidate, drill the 30-question mathematics/geometry/logic test and prepare for the 15-30 minute interview, since both are mandatory stages before final selection
As a PhD candidate, draft the research-topic proposal and the written example of research you have carried out in advance - they are compulsory uploads, not optional extras
Watch the official announcements page from late December, since the window opening is announced there rather than sent to registered candidates
common_rejection_risks: Falling below the hard percentage cut-offs for your level and field (70% undergraduate, 75% graduate, 90% for medicine, dentistry and pharmacy) or over the age limits (21/30/35)

Applying for a department or country that is not on the joint programme's published list, or forgetting to tick the joint-programme box, which silently routes the file into the general Türkiye Scholarships pool
Being currently enrolled at a Turkish university at the same level you are applying for, or holding/lost Turkish citizenship
Submitting an incomplete file before 20 February - preliminary screening removes files missing documents before any expert or interview evaluation happens
Choosing programme preferences inconsistent with your academic background, since experts explicitly score the consistency of preferences and the letter of intent
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition, dormitory fees or the graduate housing allowance, health insurance, the Turkish course and the round-trip tickets are covered, but you still fund passport and identity documents, translation and notarisation, international exam fees (TOEFL/GRE/SAT), pre-departure travel and setup, day-to-day personal expenses, and any rent above the published housing allowance (6.000 TL per month in Istanbul and Ankara, 5.000 TL elsewhere) after the first year at master's and doctoral level. Associate and bachelor's awardees ultimately repay the loan to the IsDB Education Trust after graduation and employment.
document_audit: The photograph must have been taken within the last year - an older university ID photo is a common, avoidable rejection
The diploma or temporary graduation certificate must cover the latest completed education, and originals of these documents are checked again at the interview
The research-topic proposal and written research example apply only to PhD applications - master's applicants should not waste the upload slot on them, but PhD applicants must not skip them

National exam results are 'if any' - omitting them is permitted, but international results (GRE/GMAT/SAT, TOEFL/DELF) become mandatory the moment your chosen university or programme requires them, so verify each programme individually in TBBS
alerts: The 20 February cut-off is hard in practice: incomplete or late files are screened out before expert review, and there is no published late or supplementary round

The undergraduate selection test is deliberately English-heavy for health, science and engineering applicants and includes Turkish-curriculum content, and in high-volume countries such as Afghanistan and Sudan it can run to 80-100 questions

Every awardee without a C1 Turkish certificate, including students placed in English-medium programmes, must complete the one-year preparatory course and reach C1, which adds a year to the overall timeline
Because results arrive in early August and grantees are transferred to Türkiye in September, you cannot reliably run this alongside a same-year autumn intake elsewhere
Stipend amounts and the housing allowance are published in Turkish lira, so the real value you live on depends on exchange rates at the time you arrive
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register on TBBS, complete the application answering 'Yes' to Joint Scholarship Programs, pick preferences from the programme lists offered to you, upload the documents and submit by 20 February; the file then passes preliminary screening, expert committee evaluation, a national quantitative test for undergraduate candidates, a face-to-face interview, and final selection with results in early August.
